reasoning: Set A has a richer, more faithful RL spec. It has random and scripted baselines in every environment, a tabular-then-DQN ladder where each rung adds one piece, a plain-vs-shaped reward comparison, a REINFORCE-to-PPO ladder, and a co-learning ladder with a control for each side plus a version tournament. That matches the user's goals closely. But its build plan is stale against its own architecture. AD-16 says the M1 plan must be replanned before building, and it was not. M1-T01 and M1-T03 still Read the retired `registry.make_agent`, so their context packets failed to generate: the interface task, the very first task, has no packet. The plan uses Snake-only signatures (`make_env("snake", "shaped")`, `points`, `points_after`) that the frozen contract no longer has. PL-01 steps the train loop needs (`run_streams`, `make_schedule`, `SoloSchedule`, `test_lineup`) have no M1 task and are not deferred. pipelines.md also keeps a 'routed to architecture-design' note for `train.RunStreams`, a type the architecture already added. Set B's build docs are consistent. Its 23 packets generate, its walking-skeleton M1 is a clean vertical slice, the interface task freezes every crossing type with fakes, and the dependency graph is sound. B's weaknesses are in how faithful it is to the project. It drops the random baseline the success criteria require. It adds rented-GPU spending (QR-02 '$5 per world') against the free-tools constraint. It has no reward-shaping experiment. Its tank design lets a fish see the ball only one step before contact, a flaw it admits in its own Risks. It splits a solo learning lab into 12 workspace packages, and its M4 is a leftover milestone blocked on a probe. On this rubric, A's broken first task and stale plan outweigh B's design deviations.

strengths: Strongest RL pedagogy: one-piece-at-a-time ladders for DQN, policy gradient and co-learning, each with before/after comparisons
Random and scripted baselines in every environment, matching the success criteria
Explicit reward-shaping and partial-observability (short vs wide view) experiments
Precise, testable spec with Given/When/Then for every requirement
Single package with import-linter layers suits a solo learner
weaknesses: M1 plan not replanned after AD-11/AD-16; interface and make_agent packets fail to generate
M1 has no tasks for run_streams, make_schedule/SoloSchedule or test_lineup, which train_loop needs
Process narration in the architecture ("On approval: pipeline-design updates...", "M1 is at 0 of 20 tasks")
M3 crams the whole fish-tank stage into one very large milestone

strengths: Every context packet generates and is self-contained
Walking-skeleton M1 that trains, evaluates and lists end to end, with system tasks swapping fakes for real packages
Interface task freezes all seven packages' boundary types with fixture-backed fakes
Clean dependency graph with valid edge kinds and no write collisions
weaknesses: No random baseline, though the success criteria require beating random and scripted
Rented GPU spending added against the 'no budget beyond free tools' constraint
No reward-shaping experiment; exploration only logged
Tank design lets fish see the ball only one step before contact (admitted in Risks)
12 workspace packages is over-split for a solo learning project
M4 'Fish twin' is a leftover milestone blocked on probe PB-01
